name: STM32G030F6P6TR
title: STM32G030x6/x8 Arm Cortex-M0+ microcontrollers, 64 MHz, 32 or 64 Kbytes Flash, 8 Kbytes SRAM, 2.0 V to 3.6 V
summary: A mainstream Cortex-M0+ microcontroller line running at up to 64 MHz from a single 2.0 V to 3.6 V supply, with 32 or 64 Kbytes of ECC Flash and 8 Kbytes of parity-checked SRAM. It carries a 12-bit 2.5 MSps ADC, five 16-bit timers, two USARTs, two SPIs (one with I2S), two I2Cs with Fast-mode Plus, a calendar RTC with VBAT backup, and five-channel DMA. Packages run from SO8N to LQFP48. STM32G030F6P6TR is the 32 Kbyte TSSOP20 part with 17 GPIOs, on tape and reel.

circuits.title: Power supply scheme
circuits.description: The VDD/VDDA pin takes the main 2.0 V to 3.6 V rail with one 100 nF and one 4.7 µF ceramic capacitor to VSS/VSSA, mounted at or under the pin pair. A 1.55 V to 3.6 V backup source feeds VBAT, which keeps the RTC, LSE and backup registers alive through the internal power switch. The VREF+ pin takes the ADC reference with 100 nF to ground.
notes: On packages without VBAT or VREF+ pins those nodes are bonded to VDD/VDDA inside.

circuits.title: 8 MHz crystal on the HSE oscillator
circuits.description: An 8 MHz crystal or resonator between OSC_IN and OSC_OUT with a load capacitor from each side to ground; the 200 kΩ feedback resistor is inside the chip. A series resistor REXT sits between the crystal and OSC_OUT, sized for the crystal. CL1 and CL2 are normally equal; the crystal's load capacitance is their series value, with about 10 pF of pin and board capacitance counted in.
notes: A resonator with built-in capacitors replaces Y1, C1 and C2.
Crystal and capacitors go as close to the oscillator pins as possible.

circuits.title: 32.768 kHz crystal on the LSE oscillator
circuits.description: A 32.768 kHz crystal between OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT with a load capacitor from each pin to ground, driving the RTC clock. The oscillator's drive strength is set in software (LSEDRV). No resistor goes across the crystal: one is not needed and must not be fitted.
notes: A resonator with built-in capacitors replaces Y1, C1 and C2.
Crystal and capacitors go as close to the oscillator pins as possible.

circuits.title: NRST pin protection
circuits.description: A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground, close to the chip, guards against stray resets; a push-button to ground gives a manual reset. The pull-up is inside the chip. Whatever drives NRST must be able to pull it below VIL(NRST) max or the reset is ignored.

operation.text: Arm Cortex-M0+ at up to 64 MHz: two-stage pipeline, Von Neumann bus, single-cycle multiplier, with a memory protection unit that an RTOS can use to fence tasks from each other's memory (it can also be left off).

32 or 64 Kbytes with ECC (single-bit correction, double-bit detection, failing address readable). Readout protection has three levels: 0 none; 1 blocks Flash access whenever debug is attached or the part boots from RAM or the bootloader; 2 disables debug, RAM boot and bootloader for good. Write protection covers two areas per bank in 2 Kbyte steps. Endurance 1 kcycle, retention 15 years at 85 °C.
8 Kbytes with hardware parity, accessed at CPU speed with no wait states. A parity error can trigger a timer break.

The boot pin (BOOT0 on PA14, enabled by the boot selector option bit) and the option bits choose boot from user Flash, system memory or SRAM. The system-memory bootloader reprograms Flash over USART on PA9/PA10 or PA2/PA3, or over I2C on PB6/PB7 or PB10/PB11.
Computes a CRC with a configurable polynomial and size, usable to check Flash integrity at run time against a signature stored at link time (as EN/IEC 60335-1 allows).

One pin, VDD/VDDA, supplies everything at 2.0 V to 3.6 V: the regulator and system analog (VDD), the ADC (VDDA) and the I/Os (VDDIO1). VBAT, 1.55 V to 3.6 V, keeps the RTC domain alive when VDD is gone. VREF+ is the ADC reference. An internal linear regulator makes VCORE for the logic, SRAM and Flash; Flash also draws on VDD.

VDD/VDDA to VSS/VSSA takes one 100 nF plus one 4.7 µF ceramic capacitor, placed as close to the pins as possible or underneath on the back of the board. VREF+ takes 100 nF. The 100 nF capacitor is a good-quality ceramic.
An always-on POR/PDR holds the chip in reset while VDD is below the threshold (rising 2.10 V typ, falling 2.00 V typ), so no external reset circuit is needed. Release follows a 250 µs typ delay.

The main regulator runs in Run and Sleep; Stop and both low-power run and sleep modes use the low-power regulator. Range 1 allows the full 64 MHz; Range 2 limits clocks (16 MHz system, 26 MHz HSE bypass). Both regulators are off and high-impedance in Standby.

Sleep stops only the CPU. Low-power run executes from Flash or SRAM on the low-power regulator at up to 2 MHz; Low-power sleep stops its CPU clock. Stop 0 and Stop 1 keep SRAM and registers, stop every VCORE clock and turn off the PLL, HSI16 and HSE while LSE or LSI and the RTC may run; the main regulator stays on in Stop 0 and is off in Stop 1. Standby turns VCORE off and loses all registers except the RTC domain and standby logic; each I/O can keep a pull-up or pull-down. Standby ends on NRST, IWDG, a WKUP pin edge, an RTC event or an LSE failure.

During reset the I/O Schmitt triggers are off to save power. When the reset comes from inside, the NRST pull-up is switched off. All I/Os come out of reset as analog inputs, except PA13 and PA14 which are SWDIO (pull-up) and SWCLK (pull-down).

The RTC, LSE and backup registers run from VBAT (battery or supercapacitor) when VDD is invalid, and from VDD/VDDA whenever both are valid; an internal supervisor switches between them. While VDD is valid an internal charger can charge the VBAT source through 5 kΩ or 1.5 kΩ (VBRS). External interrupts and RTC events cannot end VBAT mode.

System clock from a 4 to 48 MHz crystal or resonator (HSE, or an external clock in bypass), the 16 MHz HSI16 RC (trimmable), or the PLL (up to 64 MHz from HSE or HSI16). RTC clock from a 32.768 kHz crystal (LSE, four drive levels, or bypass), the 32 kHz LSI (±5 %, also the IWDG clock) or HSE/32. I2S, USARTs, I2Cs and ADC can run from their own kernel clocks. The clock security system falls back to HSI16 on HSE failure and also detects LSE failure. MCO outputs an internal clock; LSCO outputs LSI or LSE in every low-power mode but VBAT.

For the HSE, CL1 and CL2 are high-quality ceramics of typically 5 pF to 20 pF, usually equal. The load capacitance the crystal is specified for equals CL1 and CL2 in series; pin and board capacitance, about 10 pF as a rough figure, counts toward it. Crystal and capacitors sit as close to the oscillator pins as possible. The LSE takes no resistor across the crystal.

Each pin is set as push-pull or open-drain output, input (pull-up, pull-down or neither), analog, or alternate function. The configuration can be locked. All inputs meet CMOS and TTL levels. FT pins tolerate up to VDD + 4 V when their pulls are off. _f pins sink 20 mA for Fast-mode Plus; _a pins have the analog switch; _e pins have a switchable diode to VDD that accepts 5 mA of positive injection.

An input held at an intermediate voltage draws current through its Schmitt trigger, and a floating input can settle there or toggle from noise. Unused pins are set to analog mode or held at a fixed level by a pull or by output mode; ADC inputs are set to analog.

These pins are powered through the backup power switch, which sinks only 3 mA: as outputs they run at most 2 MHz into 30 pF and must not source current (no LED). After an RTC domain power-up their function follows the RTC registers, which system reset does not clear.
On the SO8N part PA0, PA1 and PA2 are bonded to pin 4 with NRST and stay in input mode always. Several other SO8N and TSSOP20 pins also carry two or more GPIOs bonded together.
SYSCFG_CFGR1 can put PA9 and PA10 on the PA11 and PA12 pins. On SO8N and TSSOP20, PA9 and PA10 have no pins of their own.

Five-channel DMA, each channel tied by DMAMUX to any peripheral request or a software trigger; four software priority levels, byte, half-word or word transfers with packing, circular buffers, up to 65535 items, and interrupts on half transfer, transfer complete and error. DMAMUX can also generate requests from trigger events.

The NVIC handles 32 maskable lines, the NMI and 10 core exceptions with 4 priority levels, late-arrival and tail-chaining. The EXTI routes any GPIO and some peripheral signals onto edge-detecting lines that can wake the part from Stop and records which line woke it.

12-bit SAR, up to 2.5 MSps at 12 bits from up to 16 external and 3 internal channels (temperature sensor, VREFINT, VBAT/3), single or scan mode, DMA, analog watchdog, timer triggers and hardware oversampling up to 256x for 16-bit results. Its clock is independent of the CPU and it powers down between conversions. A calibration after each power-up is recommended. Below VDDA = 2.4 V the I/O analog switch booster is turned on (BOOSTEN).

The sensor voltage rises 2.5 mV/°C typ and reads 0.76 V typ at 30 °C; its offset varies part to part, so the factory value TS_CAL1 (taken at 30 °C, 3.0 V) is used for absolute readings. VREFINT, 1.212 V typ, is measured at 30 °C and 3.0 V and the result stored as VREFINT calibration data.

TIM1: 16-bit advanced-control timer, four channels, three with complementary outputs and dead time, break inputs, PWM outputs disabled in debug. TIM3: 16-bit, four channels, quadrature encoder. TIM14: one channel. TIM16 and TIM17: one channel plus a complementary output. All count at up to 64 MHz and can be chained.

The IWDG has an 8-bit prescaler and 12-bit down-counter with a window, clocked by the LSI, keeps running in Stop and Standby, and is enabled by hardware or software option. The WWDG has a 7-bit down-counter on the system clock with an early-warning interrupt. SysTick is a 24-bit auto-reload down-counter.

BCD calendar with sub-seconds, alarm, 17-bit periodic wakeup timer, 0.95 ppm digital calibration, 50/60 Hz reference input, timestamp, and two tamper pins with filters. Five 32-bit backup registers (20 bytes) survive system reset, power reset and Standby wakeup while VBAT is valid. On LSE the RTC runs in VBAT mode; on LSI it does not.

Two I2C interfaces, Standard, Fast and Fast-mode Plus (1 Mbit/s), 7- and 10-bit addressing, clock stretching, analog and digital filters. I2C1 adds SMBus 3.0/PMBus 1.3, an independent clock and wakeup from Stop on address match. SDA and SCL are not true open-drain: the PMOS to VDDIO1 is disabled but present. Only FT_f pins meet the Fm+ sink current.

Two USARTs up to 8 Mbit/s with hardware flow control, RS485 driver enable, synchronous master mode and single-wire half duplex. USART1 adds smartcard, IrDA, LIN, Modbus, auto baud rate, receiver timeout and wakeup from Stop on start bit or frame match.

Two SPIs up to 32 Mbit/s, master or slave, 4- to 16-bit frames, NSS pulse and TI modes, hardware CRC. SPI1 also runs as I2S, master or slave, 16/24/32-bit data, sampling rates 8 kHz to 192 kHz, with a master clock output at 256 times the sampling rate.
Serial wire debug on PA13 (SWDIO) and PA14 (SWCLK).

Voltages are to VSS. Min and max are guaranteed over temperature, supply and frequency by production test at 25 °C and TA(max), or by characterization (mean ±3σ) where noted. Typical values are at 25 °C and VDD = VDDA = 3 V and are not tested. Pin parameters are measured into 50 pF.
All I/Os analog, peripherals off unless named, Flash wait states at the minimum for fHCLK, fPCLK = fHCLK when peripherals run. IDD and IDDVBAT are measured in the VDD/VDDA and VBAT lines.

The current all I/Os source plus the MCU's own VDD current stays within IVDD (100 mA); the current they sink plus the MCU's VSS current stays within IVSS (100 mA). Totals sunk and sourced by all I/Os are each limited to 80 mA.

Functional ESD tests reach class 2B and fast-transient bursts class 5A on LQFP48 at 3.3 V and 64 MHz; the device recovers through a reset. Firmware should handle a corrupted program counter, unexpected resets and corrupted control registers.
Junction-to-ambient thermal resistance (JESD51-2, still air) is 84 °C/W for LQFP48 and LQFP32, 88 °C/W for TSSOP20 and 134 °C/W for SO8N. The operating junction limit is 105 °C.

Top marking examples: LQFP48 STM32G030 / C6T6, LQFP32 STM32G / 030K6T6, TSSOP20 32G030F6P6, SO8N 32G030J6, each with a date code (Y WW), revision code and pin 1 mark. Parts marked ES or E are engineering samples, not qualified for production.
